member: Lena — Refrigeration and Thermal Insulation Engineer
message:
Surya, Farah, Kofi, the box stays cold with little leak using the 100 mm Polyurethane sandwich-panel cold box (C4), where Polyurethane (PU) means rigid foam insulation. Thick foam on a bedroom-size room lets in only a small heater worth of heat. Numbers are 2.00 by 2.00 by 2.20 m inside with 186 W conduction for 33 K lift and 376 W steady thermal per the steady cooling load and pull-down for 1 tonne box (E24), sane against a domestic freezer scaled to a room.

Surya, Farah, Kofi, the chiller size follows steady load plus slow pull-down using the Direct Current vapor-compression chiller (C5), where Direct Current (DC) means battery power and Coefficient of Performance (COP) means cooling per electric watt. A small compressor running steadily holds 4 to 10 C, but a full warm tonne cannot be cooled fast. Numbers are 150 W steady electric per the steady electric watts from COP 2.5 (E51), 3.60 kWh per day per the daily electric kWh from 150 W continuous (E52), and 50.0 h pull-down at 0.5 kW net per the pulldown hours for 25 kWh at 0.5 kW net (E53), so load in daily batches, sane against one-third of a household day.

Even air and access use the uniform low-velocity airflow (C6) with side racks and 900 mm door per the Interior plan and section (E36). Not ready, because daily warm loading rate and door openings with Farah and night energy cover with Surya are still unagreed.
